answers.explanation: One key for everyone. WPA2-Enterprise gives each user their own credentials instead.
Offline guessing has no rate limit, and the network never knows it's happening.
Simultaneous Authentication of Equals, WPA3's handshake.
SAE (commit, then confirm) makes a fresh key. The 4-way handshake then turns it into session keys.
That symmetry is the "equals" in the name.
H2E turns the password and SSID into the PWE that SAE's math is built on.
Each session's key is fresh and never sent, so old recordings stay encrypted.
AES-128 at home, AES-256 for commercial and government use.
WEP is broken by design. A long password doesn't help.
